small_guidance:
- The softmax/sigmoid kernel is already fused and cheap; the conv_transpose3d dominates the 11.4 ms runtime. Tuning BLOCK_P/BLOCK_C further (e.g. BLOCK_P=16/32, num_warps=8) will only shave the tail and cannot close the 2.4× gap to baseline.
- If keeping the torch convtranspose, at minimum ensure cudnn benchmark mode is enabled (`torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True`) and confirm channels_last_3d actually selects a faster cudnn algo for this shape — otherwise revert to contiguous, since channels_last_3d on ConvTranspose3d often falls back to slow paths on Ampere.
- Sweep BLOCK_P ∈ {16,32,64} with BLOCK_C=64 (C=64 exactly) and num_warps ∈ {4,8}; with C a power of two, drop the c_mask entirely to remove a predicate from the inner loop.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add (or gather-based) kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), compute `input × weight` outer products and accumulate into the output grid with stride=2/padding=1/output_padding=1 index math. This is where the 80%+ of runtime lives.
- Better: implement it as a gather-style direct kernel where each output element (n, oc, od, oh, ow) loops over (ic, kd, kh, kw), checks `(od + pad - kd) % stride == 0` and gathers the corresponding input voxel — then fuse the channel-wise softmax+sigmoid epilogue across OC in the same kernel (one program owns a full OC column for a spatial position, since OC=64 fits in a single tile).
- Fuse the softmax (reduction over OC=64) and sigmoid directly into the conv-transpose epilogue: have each program compute all 64 OC outputs for its spatial tile in registers, then do the max/exp/sum/sigmoid in-register and store once — eliminating the extra read+write of the full (16,64,32,64,64) tensor between conv and softmax.
